title_en: What a sleep deficit is
text_en: Most adults need at least seven hours of sleep a night, though the exact need differs from person to person. When sleep keeps falling short of that need, the shortfall builds up night after night, and only good-quality sleep can make it up.
text_ko: 성인은 대개 하루에 적어도 일곱 시간은 자야 하지만, 필요한 수면 시간은 사람마다 다르다. 필요한 만큼 자지 못하는 날이 이어지면 모자란 잠이 하루하루 쌓이며, 이렇게 쌓인 수면 부족은 질 좋은 잠을 자야만 해소된다.

sources.title: How Much Sleep Is Enough?
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B: Sleep Accommodations (NASA-STD-3001 technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

numbers: Adults: 7–9 h recommended, and under 7 h may bring more health problems (NHLBI, 2022); 7 or more h on a regular basis for ages 18–60 (AASM/SRS consensus as cited in the NASA HRP Sleep Evidence Report, 2016). With a long sleep opportunity adults average about 8.5 h, range roughly 6.1–10.3 h (same report). Sleep debt can only be repaid with good-quality sleep (OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say everyone needs exactly eight hours, or that people can get used to short sleep without harm (NHLBI calls that a myth).

title_en: Why sleep runs short in space
text_en: Crews in space have averaged about six hours of sleep a night, somewhat less than before flight. Heavy workloads, abrupt schedule shifts and unusual light–dark cycles can push the body clock out of step with the sleep period, but whether the space environment itself or mission demands matter most is not settled.
text_ko: 우주에서 승무원이 실제로 잔 시간은 하루 평균 여섯 시간 정도로, 비행 전보다 조금 짧았다. 과중한 업무와 갑작스러운 일정 변경, 지상과 다른 낮과 밤의 주기는 생체 시계를 정해진 수면 시간과 어긋나게 할 수 있다. 다만 우주 환경 자체와 임무 부담 가운데 어느 쪽의 영향이 더 큰지는 아직 밝혀지지 않았다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B: Sleep Accommodations (NASA-STD-3001 technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Risks of Human Spaceflight

numbers: In flight about 6.0 h (shuttle) and 6.1 h (ISS) per night versus 6.3–6.4 h before flight, data from 2001–2011 (NASA HRP Sleep Evidence Report, 2016); 'about six hours' regardless of mission or method, about 0.3 h a day less than three months before launch (OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B, 2023). ISS crews see 16 sunrises and sunsets a day (NASA sleep risk page).
do_not_claim: Do not say weightlessness is the proven cause of short sleep; the cause is open. The figures are from shuttle and ISS crews in 2001–2011, not from Mars missions.

title_en: Setting up the sleep space
text_en: A sleep space that is cool, with air flowing from head to foot, and shielded from noise and light can make sleep easier. Earplugs, an eye mask and extra layers to adjust warmth can help, and in weightlessness a snugly fastened sleeping bag suits people needing the feeling of being held down.
text_ko: 잠자는 공간이 서늘하고, 머리에서 발 쪽으로 공기가 흐르며, 소음과 빛이 차단되어 있으면 잠들기가 한결 쉬워질 수 있다. 귀마개와 안대를 쓰고, 덮거나 입는 것을 조절해 따뜻한 정도를 맞추는 것이 도움이 될 수 있다. 무중력에서 몸이 잠자리에 눌려 있는 느낌이 있어야 편한 사람은 침낭을 몸에 꼭 맞게 고정하는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B: Sleep Accommodations (NASA-STD-3001 technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-016: Behavioral Health and Performance (technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Hazard: Hostile/Closed Environments

numbers: ISS cabin about 18–27 °C and 30–65% humidity; sleep-area noise limits NC-50 for missions up to 30 days and NC-40 beyond (OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say these measures are proven to lengthen sleep in flight; the in-flight effectiveness of countermeasures was unknown as of the 2016 evidence report.

title_en: Light and wind-down time before sleep
text_en: Too little light, or light at the wrong time, can throw the body clock off, so space-station lighting imitates the day–night cycle on Earth. Brighter light in the work period and the dimmer setting before sleep fit this pattern. Too little wind-down time is also reported to make falling asleep harder, so that time is worth protecting.
text_ko: 빛이 모자라거나 빛을 받는 시간대가 맞지 않으면 생체 시계가 흐트러질 수 있어, 우주정거장의 조명은 지구의 낮과 밤 주기를 본뜨도록 만들어져 있다. 일하는 시간에는 밝은 조명을, 잠들기 전에는 더 어두운 조명을 쓰는 것이 이 원리에 맞다. 잠들기 전에 긴장을 풀 시간이 모자라면 잠들기 어렵다는 승무원들의 보고도 있으므로 그 시간을 지키는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

numbers: ISS LED lighting has three settings: general, alerting/shift-supporting, and pre-sleep with reduced short-wavelength light (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025; Sleep Evidence Report, 2016). In a shuttle-era survey of 74 astronauts, 54% said falling asleep was easy; the rest named too little wind-down time among the reasons (Sleep Evidence Report, 2016).
do_not_claim: Do not say lighting is proven to fix sleep in flight; in-flight effectiveness was unproven as of the 2016 report and newer evidence comes from ground analogs.

title_en: Caffeine: timing matters
text_en: Caffeine takes about half an hour to work and stays in the body for many hours, so it is better kept to the early part of the waking day. Taken later it can disturb the next sleep; in one study a large amount taken six hours before bedtime still did. It does not replace sleep.
text_ko: 카페인은 마신 뒤 삼십 분쯤 지나야 효과가 나타나고 몸속에 여러 시간 남아 있으므로, 깨어 있는 시간의 초반에 마시는 편이 좋다. 늦게 마시면 그날 잠을 방해할 수 있으며, 한 연구에서는 잠자리에 들기 여섯 시간 전에 많은 양을 섭취했을 때에도 수면이 나빠졌다. 카페인이 잠을 대신해 주지는 못한다.

key_terms.en: early part of the waking day

sources.title: Long work hours training for emergency responders: caffeine (archived page) [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
Drake et al. (caffeine taken at different times before bed)

numbers: Caffeine acts after about 30 min (15–45) and has a half-life of 5–6 h (NIOSH training page, archived). 400 mg taken at bedtime, 3 h before or 6 h before each disturbed sleep (Drake et al., 2013, abstract only). An evening dose of about 2.9 mg/kg shifted the body clock later, and a 200 mg morning dose altered deep-sleep brain activity that night (NASA HRP Sleep Evidence Report, 2016).
do_not_claim: Six hours before bed is not a guaranteed safe cut-off (it was the longest gap tested and it still disturbed sleep). Give no personal dose, and do not say caffeine treats tiredness or makes up for lost sleep.

title_en: Short planned naps
text_en: A planned nap of half an hour or less can restore wakefulness for a while. Grogginess just after waking is common and tends to be heavier after longer naps or when already short of sleep, so it helps to leave time before a demanding task. A nap does not cancel a run of short nights.
text_ko: 삼십 분을 넘기지 않게 계획해서 자는 낮잠은 한동안 정신을 또렷하게 해 줄 수 있다. 잠에서 깬 직후에는 멍한 상태가 흔히 나타나는데, 낮잠이 길수록, 또 이미 잠이 모자란 상태일수록 더 심한 편이므로 중요한 작업 전에는 시간 여유를 두는 것이 좋다. 낮잠을 잔다고 해서 여러 날 쌓인 수면 부족이 없어지지는 않는다.

sources.title: Work-hour training for nurses, Module 7: naps at work (archived page) [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Work-hour training for nurses, Module 7: sleep inertia (archived page) [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B: Sleep Accommodations (NASA-STD-3001 technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

numbers: A nap of about 30 min can raise alertness on night shift (NIOSH, archived page). Laboratory work cited in the NASA HRP Sleep Evidence Report (2016): a 10-min nap gave little grogginess, a 30-min nap could impair performance for up to an hour, and a 60-min nap at 04:00 left night workers worse than no nap. Grogginess after waking: typically 30–60 min, seen up to 2 h (NIOSH) versus gradual fading over roughly 2–4 h (NASA report); the sources differ.
do_not_claim: Sources differ on how long grogginess after waking lasts and on whether a half-hour nap is free of it, so give no single ideal nap length. Do not quote the popular '26-minute NASA nap' percentages; they were not in the abstract the notes read.

title_en: Feeling fine is not a reliable gauge
text_en: When nights stay short, performance keeps slipping with each further night, while the feeling of sleepiness rises only a little and then levels off. People can therefore be more impaired than they feel, so it is worth looking at how the last several nights have gone, not only at how awake one feels.
text_ko: 잠을 짧게 자는 날이 이어지면 업무 수행 능력은 날이 갈수록 계속 떨어지지만, 졸리다는 느낌은 조금 커지다가 더는 커지지 않는다. 그래서 스스로 느끼는 것보다 실제 능력이 더 떨어져 있을 수 있다. 지금 정신이 얼마나 또렷하게 느껴지는지만 보지 말고 최근 며칠 동안 얼마나 잤는지도 함께 살펴보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
Van Dongen et al. (chronic sleep restriction experiment)

numbers: Healthy adults limited to 6 h or 4 h in bed for 14 nights showed steadily accumulating deficits comparable to up to two nights without sleep, while their sleepiness ratings rose only a little (Van Dongen et al., 2003, abstract only; summarised in the NASA HRP Sleep Evidence Report, 2016).
do_not_claim: Do not say people adapt to short sleep. Do not give an 'hours awake equals a blood-alcohol level' equivalence; the sources differ (17 versus 19 hours).

title_en: Short sleep shows up in mood and teamwork too
text_en: Short sleep can slow reactions and make it harder to focus and to read other people's emotions. Mood can dip, and irritability, blaming and poorer communication within a team have been linked to sleep loss. Changes like these are worth noticing after a poor night.
text_ko: 잠이 모자라면 반응이 느려지고, 집중하기 어려워지며, 다른 사람의 감정을 알아차리기도 힘들어질 수 있다. 기분이 가라앉을 수 있고, 짜증이 늘거나 남을 탓하게 되고 팀 안의 의사소통이 나빠지는 것도 수면 부족과 관련이 있다고 알려져 있다. 잠을 설친 다음 날에는 이런 변화가 있는지 살펴보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: What Are Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency?
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
OCHMO-TB-041 Rev B: Sleep Accommodations (NASA-STD-3001 technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Hazard: Isolation and Confinement
Jones et al. (ISS sleep, self-ratings and reaction self-test)

numbers: In NASA's HERA analog, sleep restriction was associated with worse emotion recognition and slower, less accurate sustained attention (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025). In ISS astronauts, nights under 6 h were linked to slower reaction speed and higher stress ratings (Jones et al., 2022, abstract only).
do_not_claim: Do not present these changes as proof that poor sleep is the cause, or as a diagnosis; the same changes have other causes.

title_en: When to raise short sleep with the CMO
text_en: If sleep keeps falling short despite your own efforts, it is reasonable to tell the CMO or ground medical staff. In spaceflight, flight doctors and mission planners have adjusted schedules case by case so that crew members get enough sleep and time off.
text_ko: 스스로 노력해도 잠이 계속 모자라면 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알리는 것이 좋다. 우주 비행에서는 승무원이 충분히 자고 쉴 수 있도록 담당 의사와 임무 운영진이 상황에 맞추어 일정을 조정해 왔다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload

do_not_claim: No public NASA threshold (hours of sleep or number of nights) for contacting the flight surgeon about sleep was found, so do not state one. Naming the CMO and ground medical staff as the contacts on a Mars mission is the knowledge-base author's adaptation of the source guidance (which speaks of flight surgeons or health providers), not a published NASA procedure. The cited practice is flight surgeons adjusting schedules with operations staff.

title_en: What a wrist device can and cannot tell about sleep
title_ko: 손목 기기의 수면 기록으로 알 수 있는 것과 없는 것
text_en: A wrist device estimates sleep from how still the arm is. It picks up real sleep well but often counts lying awake without moving as sleep, so it tends to show more sleep than was actually had. It cannot diagnose a sleep problem, and how well it works in weightlessness has not been established.
text_ko: 손목에 차는 기기는 팔이 얼마나 가만히 있는지를 바탕으로 수면을 추정한다. 실제로 잠든 시간은 잘 찾아내지만 깬 채로 가만히 누워 있는 시간도 잠으로 세는 일이 많아, 수면 시간을 실제보다 길게 보여 주는 경향이 있다. 이 기록만으로 수면 문제를 진단할 수는 없으며, 무중력에서 얼마나 정확한지도 아직 확인되지 않았다.

sources.title: de Zambotti et al. (wearable sleep technology review)
Khosla et al. (American Academy of Sleep Medicine position statement on consumer sleep technology)
Chinoy et al. (seven consumer sleep trackers compared with laboratory sleep recording)
Ongoing HRP Research in Space

numbers: Wrist devices detect sleep with sensitivity above 90% but detect wakefulness with specificity of only about 27–77% in healthy people (de Zambotti et al., 2019). Seven consumer devices against laboratory sleep recording: sensitivity at least 0.93, wake specificity 0.18–0.54, inconsistent sleep-stage estimates, worse on disrupted nights (Chinoy et al., 2021, abstract only). Consumer sleep technology cannot be used to diagnose or treat sleep disorders (Khosla et al., 2018, abstract only). A wrist actigraphy device recording motion, sleep patterns and light exposure is used on Artemis II (NASA Ongoing HRP Research page).
do_not_claim: Do not state a wearable sleep total as exact, report sleep-stage percentages, or say the reading detects a condition. 'Not established in weightlessness' means the research notes found no validation study in microgravity, not that a study showed it fails.

title_en: Why mood can dip in long isolation
title_ko: 오랜 고립 생활에서 기분이 가라앉는 이유
text_en: Living for a long time in a small, isolated space can bring low mood, worry, irritability and friction with others, and may affect sleep, morale and decision-making. In past spaceflight such changes have mostly been mild, although they are thought to be under-reported.
text_ko: 고립되고 좁은 공간에서 오래 생활하면 기분이 가라앉거나 불안해지고, 짜증이 늘거나 동료와 마찰이 생길 수 있으며, 수면과 사기, 의사 결정에도 영향을 줄 수 있다. 지금까지의 우주 비행에서 이런 변화는 대부분 가벼운 수준이었지만, 실제보다 적게 보고되었을 가능성이 있다.

sources.title: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Human Research Roadmap: behavioral risk page

numbers: Shuttle missions 1981–1989: 34 behavioral signs or symptoms among 208 crew members (about one per 2.87 person-years), most often anxiety and annoyance; ISS Expeditions 1–40: 0.62 per person-year in flight-surgeon records, a figure the report calls probably low (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025). In-flight symptoms have not reached a diagnostic threshold (NASA Human Research Roadmap, 2025).
do_not_claim: Do not say the person has depression or an anxiety disorder, and do not read the low recorded rate as low risk (under-reporting is acknowledged).

title_en: What wears mood down and what protects it
title_ko: 기분을 끌어내리는 요인과 지켜 주는 요인
text_en: Monotony, a workload that is too heavy or too light, missing family, poor sleep and physical discomfort can each wear mood down on a long mission. Meaningful work, time looking out of a window, and giving and receiving support tend to protect it.
text_ko: 긴 임무에서는 단조로운 일상, 너무 많거나 너무 적은 업무, 가족과 떨어져 지내는 것, 잠을 충분히 자지 못하는 것, 몸의 불편함이 저마다 기분을 끌어내릴 수 있다. 반대로 보람 있는 일, 창밖을 바라보는 시간, 서로 도움을 주고받는 것은 기분을 지켜 주는 편이다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
OCHMO-TB-016: Behavioral Health and Performance (technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

do_not_claim: Do not single out one factor as the cause of a crew member's mood. ('수면 부족' is avoided here only because it is another condition's display name.)

title_en: Talk to the right person
text_en: Support tends to help most when it comes from the people closest to the problem: a crewmate for work stress, family for worries about home. Sharing concerns instead of holding them in, and using the scheduled private talks with family and with medical or psychological staff, are part of how crews are supported.
text_ko: 도움은 고민의 종류에 맞는 사람에게서 받을 때 효과가 큰 편이다. 그래서 업무 스트레스는 동료와, 집안 걱정은 가족과 나누는 것이 좋다. 걱정을 혼자 담아 두지 않고 털어놓는 것, 정해진 가족 대화 시간과 의료·심리 담당자와의 비공개 상담을 활용하는 것도 승무원을 위해 마련된 지원 방법이다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
CONNECT graphic (NP-2020-05-013-JSC)
Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Hazard: Distance from Earth

numbers: Private psychological conferences are normally held every 2 weeks for at least 15 minutes (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025). One-way communication delay on a Mars mission can reach about 20 minutes (NASA Hazard: Distance from Earth).
do_not_claim: Do not promise real-time video calls: on a Mars mission communication delay makes live contact with family and medical staff harder.

title_en: Exercise and a steady routine
text_en: Aerobic exercise can ease depressive and anxious feelings, especially when they are mild, and physically active members of Antarctic winter crews kept a steadier mood. Keeping regular times for meals, sleep and exercise is part of the same advice.
text_ko: 유산소 운동은 우울감과 불안을 덜어 주는 것으로 알려져 있으며, 증상이 가벼울 때 효과가 특히 뚜렷하다. 남극 기지에서 겨울을 난 대원들 가운데서도 신체 활동이 많았던 사람의 기분이 더 안정적이었다. 식사와 수면, 운동 시간을 규칙적으로 지키는 것도 함께 권장된다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
CONNECT graphic (NP-2020-05-013-JSC)
I'm So Stressed Out! (fact sheet)

numbers: Antarctic winter crews were followed over 8 months (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025). General advice: 30 minutes of walking a day can lift mood (NIMH).
do_not_claim: Do not present exercise as treatment for a diagnosed disorder or promise an effect for an individual.

title_en: Journal, window, plants and personal time
title_ko: 일지 쓰기, 창밖 보기, 식물 가꾸기
text_en: Keeping a journal is an encouraged form of self-care for isolated crews and a common outlet for stress. Looking out of a window can ease monotony and the sense of confinement, and tending plants or playing music are other ways crews have used personal time to recover.
text_ko: 일지를 쓰는 것은 고립된 환경에서 지내는 승무원에게 권장되는 자기 관리 방법이며, 스트레스를 푸는 방법으로도 흔히 쓰인다. 창밖을 바라보면 단조로움과 갇혀 있다는 느낌이 줄어들 수 있다. 식물을 가꾸거나 악기를 연주하는 것도 승무원들이 개인 시간에 기운을 되찾으려고 써 온 방법이다.

sources.title: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
OCHMO-TB-016: Behavioral Health and Performance (technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

do_not_claim: Do not promise that any one activity will lift mood; these are supports in use, not proven treatments.

title_en: Signs worth noticing
text_en: Low mood does not always look like sadness: some people mainly become irritable or angry. Other signs are losing interest in things, low energy, trouble concentrating or deciding, sleeping or eating more or less than usual, and pulling back from crewmates or from contact with the ground.
text_ko: 기분 저하가 늘 슬픔으로만 나타나는 것은 아니어서, 주로 짜증이나 화가 느는 사람도 있다. 흥미를 잃거나, 기운이 없거나, 집중하고 결정하기가 어렵거나, 잠이나 식사가 평소보다 늘거나 줄어드는 것도 눈여겨볼 변화이다. 동료나 지상과의 교류를 피하게 되는 것도 그 가운데 하나이다.

sources.title: Depression
Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

do_not_claim: These signs do not establish depression; a diagnosis needs symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks and is made by a clinician.

title_en: Does it pass, or does it stay?
text_en: Stress usually eases once the situation behind it is resolved, whereas anxiety can persist even with no present threat. A rough day is different from a mood that stays low most of the day, nearly every day, for a couple of weeks, so it is worth noting how long a change lasts.
text_ko: 스트레스는 원인이 된 상황이 해결되면 대개 가라앉지만, 불안은 당장 위협이 없어도 계속될 수 있다. 하루 이틀 힘든 것과, 가라앉은 기분이 거의 매일, 하루 대부분 이어지면서 두 주쯤 계속되는 것은 다르다. 그러므로 변화가 얼마나 오래 이어지는지 기록해 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: I'm So Stressed Out! (fact sheet)
Depression

numbers: A diagnosis of depression requires symptoms most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks (NIMH Depression, 2024).
do_not_claim: The assistant does not diagnose. Two weeks is a criterion clinicians use, not a rule that a shorter spell of low mood can be ignored.

title_en: When to tell the CMO or ground medical staff
title_ko: CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: It is time to tell the CMO or ground medical staff when low mood or worry gets in the way of work or daily life, leads to avoiding tasks or people, or seems to be there all the time. Any thoughts of death or suicide should be reported to the CMO immediately.
text_ko: 가라앉은 기분이나 불안 때문에 업무나 일상생활에 지장이 생기거나, 해야 할 일이나 사람을 피하게 되거나, 그런 상태가 늘 이어지는 것처럼 느껴지면 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 한다. 죽음에 대한 생각이나 자살 생각이 든다면 즉시 CMO에게 알려야 한다.

sources.title: I'm So Stressed Out! (fact sheet)
Depression

do_not_claim: No public NASA criterion for when a crew member should escalate a mood concern was found; this rests on NIMH general guidance. Naming the CMO and ground medical staff as the contacts on a Mars mission is the knowledge-base author's adaptation of the source guidance (which speaks of flight surgeons or health providers), not a published NASA procedure.

title_en: What skin conductance (EDA) can and cannot tell
title_ko: 피부전도도(EDA)로 알 수 있는 것과 없는 것
text_en: Electrodermal activity is the skin's electrical conductance, which rises as sweat glands become more active under the sympathetic nervous system. A rise suggests that the body is more aroused or sweating more, but not why: heat, exercise, movement and focused attention raise it too. It cannot show stress or mood by itself.
text_ko: 피부전도도(EDA)는 피부에 전기가 얼마나 잘 통하는지를 나타내는 값으로, 교감신경의 작용으로 땀샘 활동이 늘면 높아진다. 값이 오르면 몸이 더 각성된 상태이거나 땀이 늘었다고 볼 수는 있지만, 더위나 운동, 몸의 움직임, 집중만으로도 오르기 때문에 그 이유까지는 알 수 없다. 따라서 이 값만으로 스트레스나 기분 상태를 알 수는 없다.

sources.title: Posada-Quintero & Chon (review of electrodermal activity methods)
Menghini et al. (validation of a wrist-worn sensor)

numbers: In a validation of a research-grade wristband against finger electrodes in 40 people, wrist skin conductance showed no correlation with the finger signal (Menghini et al., 2019, abstract only).
do_not_claim: Do not say 'your stress level is high' from EDA, and do not say a flat reading shows calm. No wearable signal is validated for measuring mood, and the research notes found no validation of wrist EDA in weightlessness. EDA is not mentioned in the official challenge resources.

title_en: Mood over a long mission has no fixed timetable
title_ko: 긴 임무의 기분 변화에는 정해진 시간표가 없다
text_en: Mood and morale can rise and fall over a long mission, and the pattern differs widely from person to person. Studies do not agree on when a low point tends to come, so it makes sense to follow one's own trend over time and not the stage of the mission.
text_ko: 긴 임무 동안 기분과 사기는 오르내릴 수 있고, 그 양상은 사람마다 크게 다르다. 가장 힘든 시기가 언제쯤 오는지에 대해서는 연구 결과가 일치하지 않는다. 그러므로 임무가 얼마나 지났는지를 따지기보다 자신의 기분이 시간에 따라 어떻게 변해 왔는지를 살펴보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
Basner et al. (Mars-500 psychology and behavior)
Bell, Brown & Mitchell (systematic review of analog team dynamics)

numbers: ISS astronaut journals: morale tended to dip in the third quarter of an expedition and recover in the last, but the same report calls the existence of time-dependent phases an open question; some Antarctic work puts the symptom peak just after mid-mission, other work shows stress rising to the end (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025). A systematic review of 72 analog sources found that team mood did not consistently follow a third-quarter pattern (Bell et al., 2019, abstract only). Mars-500: one of six crew members reported depressive symptoms in 93% of mission weeks, two showed no disturbance (Basner et al., 2014).
do_not_claim: Do not state that a 'third-quarter' dip is a rule of long missions: sources disagree on whether and when a low point occurs.

title_en: How a crisis comes about
text_en: Thoughts of suicide have no single cause and can affect people of any background. A crisis often comes when stresses build beyond a person's ability to cope, and a sense of isolation, a loss or a conflict is closely linked with it. Stigma keeps many people from asking for help.
text_ko: 자살 생각은 한 가지 원인으로 생기지 않으며, 어떤 배경을 가진 사람에게도 생길 수 있다. 위기는 스트레스가 감당할 수 있는 정도를 넘어설 때 찾아오는 경우가 많고, 고립감이나 상실, 갈등과 밀접한 관련이 있다. 사회적 낙인이 두려워 도움을 청하지 못하는 사람도 많다.

sources.title: Suicide Prevention (health topic page)
Suicide (fact sheet)
Framework for Successful Messaging: Safety [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
sources.publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention

do_not_claim: Do not present suicide as a common, understandable or acceptable response to mission stress, and do not give a single simple cause. No data on suicidal thoughts in astronauts or analog crews were found.

title_en: What has preceded severe distress in spaceflight
title_ko: 우주 비행에서 보고된 심한 마음의 고통
text_en: Serious behavioral crises have been rare in spaceflight. Where severe distress has been described, it followed painful events such as news of a death in the family or a major setback at work, and showed as withdrawal from others and despondency.
text_ko: 우주 비행에서 심각한 정신건강 위기는 드물었다. 심한 마음의 고통이 보고된 사례에서는 가족의 사망 소식이나 업무에서의 큰 실패 같은 괴로운 일이 먼저 있었고, 그 뒤 다른 사람과의 교류를 끊거나 깊이 낙담하는 모습이 나타났다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
OCHMO-TB-016: Behavioral Health and Performance (technical brief)
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer

numbers: No behavioral emergency needing major intervention or evacuation has occurred among U.S. career astronauts in flight; shuttle payload specialists, selected and trained differently, did report such events (NASA HRP Behavioral Evidence Report, 2025; OCHMO-TB-016, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say such crises never happen in space or that trained crews are immune: under-reporting is acknowledged and no data on suicidal thoughts in crews were found. Give no identifying detail of individual cases.

title_en: Signs in what a person says
text_en: Signs to take seriously in what a person says include talk of wanting to die, of being a burden to others, or of great guilt or shame. So does talk of feeling hopeless, trapped, empty or without a reason to live, or of pain that feels unbearable.
text_ko: 죽고 싶다는 말, 자신이 다른 사람에게 짐이 된다는 말, 심한 죄책감이나 수치심을 드러내는 말은 가볍게 넘기지 말아야 할 신호이다. 희망이 없다거나, 갇힌 것 같다거나, 공허하다거나, 살 이유가 없다거나, 견딜 수 없이 고통스럽다는 말도 마찬가지이다.

sources.title: Warning Signs of Suicide
Warning Signs [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Warning Signs of Suicide [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: These signs do not measure how high the risk is, and their absence, or a calm or joking manner, does not show that a person is safe. Everyday idioms that merely contain words about dying are not signs by themselves.

title_en: Signs in behavior, and when they weigh more
text_en: Changes in behavior can also be signs: pulling away from others, saying goodbye, giving away valued belongings, taking dangerous risks, extreme mood swings, or sleeping and eating much more or less. They weigh more when the behavior is new, is increasing, or follows a painful event, loss or change.
text_ko: 행동의 변화도 신호가 될 수 있다. 사람들을 피하거나, 작별 인사를 하거나, 아끼던 물건을 나누어 주거나, 위험한 행동을 하거나, 감정 기복이 심해지거나, 잠과 식사가 크게 늘거나 줄어드는 것이 그 예이다. 이런 행동이 새로 나타났거나, 점점 늘거나, 괴로운 사건이나 상실, 큰 변화 뒤에 나타났다면 더 무겁게 받아들여야 한다.

sources.title: Warning Signs of Suicide
Warning Signs [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: A change in sleep or eating alone is non-specific; do not treat a single sign, or any wearable reading, as showing suicidal thinking.

title_en: Asking directly does not raise the risk
text_en: If you are worried about a crewmate, ask directly and calmly whether they are thinking about suicide. Studies show that asking does not put the idea into a person's head or raise the risk. Take the answer seriously.
text_ko: 동료가 걱정되면 자살을 생각하고 있는지 차분하게 직접 물어본다. 이렇게 묻는다고 해서 없던 생각이 생기거나 위험이 커지지 않는다는 것이 연구로 확인되어 있다. 돌아온 대답은 진지하게 받아들인다.

sources.title: 5 Action Steps to Help Someone Having Thoughts of Suicide
How the 5 Steps Can Help [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Help Someone Else [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: Never say or imply that asking about suicide plants the idea; the evidence is the opposite.

title_en: Stay and listen without judging
text_en: Stay with the person and listen without judging: let them finish, accept what they feel, and show that you care. Arguing about right and wrong, lecturing about the value of life, acting shocked or offering quick reassurance does not help.
text_ko: 곁에 있으면서 판단하지 말고 들어 준다. 말을 끝까지 듣고, 그 사람이 느끼는 감정을 그대로 받아들이며, 마음을 쓰고 있다는 것을 보여 준다. 옳고 그름을 따지거나, 생명의 소중함을 훈계하거나, 충격받은 모습을 보이거나, 섣불리 괜찮을 거라고 달래는 것은 도움이 되지 않는다.

sources.title: 5 Action Steps to Help Someone Having Thoughts of Suicide
Help Someone Else [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
How the 5 Steps Can Help [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: The assistant must not lecture ('you have so much to live for'), debate, or sound shocked; guidance is to help the person find their own reasons for living, not to supply them.

title_en: Check in again afterwards
text_en: Support does not end with one conversation. Checking in again afterwards, even with a short message or visit, is one of the recommended steps and can lower the risk.
text_ko: 한 번 이야기를 나눈 것으로 도움이 끝나는 것은 아니다. 그 뒤에도 짧은 메시지를 보내거나 찾아가 안부를 다시 묻는 것이 권장되는 단계이며, 이렇게 하면 위험을 낮출 수 있다.

sources.title: 5 Action Steps to Help Someone Having Thoughts of Suicide
How the 5 Steps Can Help [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: A later check-in supplements telling the CMO; it does not replace it. Naming the CMO, a trusted crewmate and ground medical staff as the contacts is the researcher's inference for a Mars mission, not a published NASA procedure.

title_en: Tell the CMO now, and do not promise secrecy
title_ko: 즉시 CMO에게 알리고 비밀을 약속하지 않는다
text_en: Thoughts of suicide or of harming oneself, whether your own or a crewmate's, should be shared immediately with the CMO or a trusted crewmate, and with ground medical staff. Because replies from the ground are delayed, tell someone on board first. Do not promise to keep it secret.
text_ko: 자살 생각이나 자해하려는 생각이 들면, 자신의 일이든 동료의 일이든 즉시 CMO나 믿을 수 있는 동료에게 알리고 지상 의료진에게도 알려야 한다. 지상의 답변은 늦게 도착하므로 먼저 함께 있는 사람에게 알린다. 비밀로 해 주겠다고 약속해서는 안 된다.

Hazard: Distance from Earth

numbers: One-way communication delay on a Mars mission can reach about 20 minutes (NASA Hazard: Distance from Earth).
do_not_claim: The U.S. phone lines named in the source guidance (988, 911) do not exist on a Mars mission. Naming the CMO, a trusted crewmate and ground medical staff as the contacts is the researcher's inference for a Mars mission, not a published NASA procedure. Do not guarantee confidentiality, and do not say the assistant can assess or rule out risk.

title_en: If there is a plan, stay close and tell the CMO at once
title_ko: 계획이 있다면 곁을 지키고 즉시 알린다
text_en: Ask whether the person has a plan. The more specific the plan, the more serious the situation, and the CMO should be told immediately. Stay with the person, and help keep anything they might use to harm themselves out of reach.
text_ko: 구체적인 계획이 있는지 물어본다. 계획이 구체적일수록 상황이 심각하므로 즉시 CMO에게 알려야 한다. 그 사람 곁을 지키면서, 자신을 해치는 데 쓸 수 있는 것을 가까이 두지 않도록 돕는다.

key_terms.ko: 자신을 해치는 데 쓸 수 있는 것

How the 5 Steps Can Help [undated page; year given is the year it was read]
Framework for Successful Messaging: Safety [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

do_not_claim: Never describe methods or name any means on board. The assistant cannot judge the level of risk; that belongs to the CMO and ground medical staff. Naming the CMO, a trusted crewmate and ground medical staff as the contacts is the researcher's inference for a Mars mission, not a published NASA procedure (no public space-agency procedure for a suicidal crisis was found).

title_en: What devices and questionnaires cannot tell
title_ko: 기기와 설문으로는 알 수 없는 것
text_en: No wearable signal is known to show or rule out thoughts of suicide; a change in sleep or appetite is only one non-specific sign among many. Even validated screening questions are a first step that hands over to a trained clinician, so what a person says and does matters most.
text_ko: 웨어러블 기기의 신호 가운데 자살 생각이 있는지 없는지를 알려 준다고 확인된 것은 없으며, 잠이나 식욕의 변화는 여러 신호 가운데 하나일 뿐 그것만으로는 판단할 수 없다. 검증된 선별 질문도 훈련받은 전문가의 평가로 이어지는 첫 단계일 뿐이다. 그러므로 그 사람의 말과 행동을 살피는 것이 가장 중요하다.

sources.title: Warning Signs of Suicide
Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) Toolkit [undated page; year given is the year it was read]

numbers: NIMH's Ask Suicide-Screening Questions tool uses four yes/no questions taking about 20 seconds; a positive screen leads to a brief safety assessment by a trained clinician (NIMH ASQ Toolkit).
do_not_claim: Do not say a wearable pattern indicates or excludes suicidal thinking, or that the assistant can assess or clear risk. The first sentence reflects that none of the sources read offers a physiological marker.
